briefs.headline: Kansas beats West Virginia 86-82 in the Players Era semifinal despite Sadler's 34
briefs.summary: No. 11 Kansas defeated West Virginia 86-82 at Michelob Ultra Arena in Las Vegas on Wednesday night in the semifinals of the Players Era tournament, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story. West Virginia led 49-44 at the half and 68-58 with 11:15 to play before a 10-2 Kansas run, and still led 82-81 with 1:26 left when Tre White was fouled twice and made four free throws in the final 39.6 seconds. Freshman Miles Sadler scored 34 points on 11 of 23 shooting with 10 of 11 free throws and Martin Somerville hit four threes for 16 off the bench, but the Mountaineers were 6 of 29 from three and were called for 30 fouls; Kansas went 27 of 40 at the line to West Virginia's 24 of 27, with White scoring 21, Trey Kaufman-Renn 19 and Keanu Dawes 18 points and 12 rebounds. Kansas is 5-0 and meets Houston, which defeated No. 1 Florida 86-76 earlier Wednesday, in Thursday's final; West Virginia, 4-1, plays Florida in the third-place game Thursday at 2:30 p.m. ET on ESPN. The game did not count in the Big 12 standings, and the teams meet again at Allen Fieldhouse on Jan. 2.

briefs.headline: Ohio beats Morehead State 91-77 behind Paveletzke's 24 points and 8 assists
briefs.summary: Ohio defeated Morehead State 91-77 at the Convocation Center in Athens on Wednesday night before 2,023, per ESPN's box score. The Bobcats led 46-45 at the half and pulled away with an 11-0 run to 75-61; Jackson Paveletzke scored 24 points on 9 of 11 shooting with eight assists, Javan Simmons had 18 points and nine rebounds and Dusan Makitan 16, and Ohio shot 54.1% from the floor with 54 points in the paint and 17 assists on 33 baskets. Clayton Parker scored 21 and Chase Dawson 20 for Morehead State, which is 3-3 and 0-3 on the road. Ohio is 3-1 and next plays New Mexico State in the Jacksonville Classic on Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 11 a.m. ET, then Rice there on Wednesday at 11 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Chelsea's Martinez starts for Argentina in 7-0 win, first match since jaw surgery
briefs.summary: Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez started for Argentina in a 7-0 friendly win over Costa Rica in Cordoba on Tuesday, per ESPN's match lineup, his first game since surgery on the jaw he broke in a collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite on Oct. 16. ESPN reported Monday that coach Lionel Scaloni had confirmed Martinez would play wearing a protective mask; Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso had left him out of the Nov. 8 loss to Sunderland, calling a return before the international break too rash and too risky. Chelsea host Leeds on Saturday at 10 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: NFL moves Raiders at Browns on Nov. 29 into the Sunday Night Football slot
briefs.summary: The NFL flexed the Las Vegas Raiders' Nov. 29 game at Cleveland into NBC's Sunday Night Football window, the league announced Tuesday, per ESPN; the Browns' schedule page now lists kickoff at 8:20 p.m. ET in place of the 1 p.m. ET slot Wednesday's paper carried. Cleveland is six wins and four losses, the AFC's seventh seed and the holder of the conference's last wild-card spot, and is four wins and no losses at home for the first time since 1963; the Raiders are four and six. The game replaces New England at the Los Angeles Chargers, which moves to 4:05 p.m. ET. The Browns are on their bye this week.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati reported near a deal to move NWSL's Racing Louisville to Cincinnati
briefs.summary: ESPN reported Tuesday, citing multiple sources, that the ownership groups of FC Cincinnati and the NWSL's Racing Louisville are nearing an agreement that would move the women's team to Cincinnati for the 2028 season, with Racing playing 2027 in Louisville and then at TQL Stadium; no agreement has been finalized and no price was reported. Racing Louisville said in a statement Tuesday that it is actively working through a process to sell the club to a new ownership group, without naming a buyer, and an FC Cincinnati spokesperson said the club is exploring opportunities to expand its involvement in women's soccer and hopes to have an update in the near future. FC Cincinnati plays its MLS Cup Playoffs Wild Card match at Orlando City on Thursday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Spurs rule Dylan Harper out of Thursday's game against the Clippers with hip soreness
briefs.summary: The Spurs ruled guard Dylan Harper out of Thursday's home game against the LA Clippers with left hip soreness, ESPN reported Wednesday evening, after his feet slid out from under him with 1:07 left in Tuesday's 105 to 93 loss to Detroit; he stayed down about a minute and was helped off the court. Harper had 20 points, four rebounds and two assists in 35 minutes against the Pistons and is averaging 18.4 points, 5.4 rebounds and 4.5 assists in his second season. San Antonio did not play Wednesday and is 12 wins and three losses, a half-game behind the Lakers in the West after Los Angeles lost at Utah; the Clippers are four and nine. Tipoff is 8 p.m. ET at the Frost Bank Center.

briefs.headline: Mexico beats Jamaica 1-0 to set up a March Nations League semifinal with the USMNT
briefs.summary: Mexico defeated Jamaica 1-0 in Monterrey on Tuesday night in the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal, per ESPN, and advanced on away goals with the series level at three goals apiece after Jamaica won the first leg 3-2 at home, so the United States' semifinal opponent in late March at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif., is Mexico rather than Jamaica. Jesus Corona scored in the 35th minute, his first international goal since September 2021, for Rafael Marquez's first win as Mexico coach after five matches without one; Panama play Canada in the other semifinal. The U.S. completed an 8-0 aggregate win over Haiti in Cincinnati the same night in Mauricio Pochettino's final game before taking the Manchester United job, and ESPN's account of his departure named no successor.

briefs.headline: Wakamotoharu wins a 10th straight and leads the Kyushu basho alone at 11 wins after day 12
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association's tournament leaders page lists maegashira (rank-and-file) 7 Wakamotoharu alone at 11 wins and one loss after day 12 of the Kyushu basho (tournament) in Fukuoka on Thursday, with three rikishi (wrestlers) one behind at 10 and two: yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato, sekiwake Atamifuji and maegashira 7 Kinbozan. Per the SumoDB results table for the day, Wakamotoharu forced out komusubi Yoshinofuji by yorikiri (frontal force-out) for his 10th win in a row since a day-two loss; Onosato pushed out ozeki (champion) Kirishima, who has lost three straight and is eight and four; Atamifuji pushed out ozeki Aonishiki, who fell to six and six; and Kinbozan threw maegashira 14 Dewanoryu with a shitatedashinage (underarm pulling throw), dropping him to eight and four. Yokozuna Hoshoryu reached seven and five with a kotenage (armlock throw) over sekiwake Fujinokawa, and ozeki Kotozakura forced out maegashira 4 Takerufuji to go seven and five; Asanoyama, Roga, Nishikifuji, Takanosho, Asahakuryu and Tamawashi join Kirishima and Dewanoryu at eight wins, a kachi-koshi (winning record). In juryo (the second division) Wakatakakage forced out Asahifuji in a meeting of the two leaders and stands alone at 11 and one. Three days remain; the final day is Sunday, Nov. 22.

briefs.headline: Jazz upset the Lakers and the Nuggets rally from 17 down past the Celtics
briefs.summary: Utah, three wins and 13 losses coming in, defeated the Lakers 109 to 97 in Salt Lake City on Wednesday behind Keyonte George's 30 points, per ESPN's scoreboard, dropping Los Angeles to 13 wins and three losses and leaving San Antonio a half-game off the top of the West. Denver came from 17 down to win 105 to 101 at Boston on Nikola Jokic's 24 points and Jamal Murray's 21; Memphis won 124 to 121 at Cleveland for a franchise-record eighth straight road win; Miami won 137 to 130 at Milwaukee in Giannis Antetokounmpo's first game against the Bucks, who have lost 11 in a row and are one and 14; Dallas, with 33 from Cooper Flagg, won 116 to 94 at Golden State, which has not won since Stephen Curry's injury; and Philadelphia, 13 and three, held the East lead with a 121 to 116 win over Orlando. Houston lost Alperen Sengun to injury in a 119 to 104 win over Indiana.

waters.reading: 99.1 cfs, 1.63 feet at 5:15 a.m., rising on flow and steady on stage against 92.1 cfs and 1.59 feet in the fetcher's 24-hour comparison.
waters.working: The gauge at Dyer reads 99.1 cfs and rising, 7 cfs over the fetcher's 24-hour comparison and about 2 cfs over the 97.3 Wednesday's paper carried at the same hour, with the stage up four hundredths to 1.63 feet; a nudge, not a bump, and still inside the late-autumn base flow the river has held all week. At 99 cfs and clear it is a long-leader, small-fly problem, with the fish on the pocket-water lies and the tailouts rather than the seams, and after another cold night the midday hours fish best once the sun is on the water. A size 18 to 20 midge or a small Blue-winged Olive nymph under a soft indicator on a long leader through the slower pockets and the tailouts is the pattern, a stonefly nymph as the point fly in the deeper plunge pools where the larger fish hold in cold water, and a sculpin pattern swung tight to the undercut banks in the first and last hour of light.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 25.01 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 24.96 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 25.0 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Normal pool with ordinary bank access, steady on the fetcher's 24-hour comparison and 22 hundredths over the 24.79 Wednesday's paper carried, so Tuesday-to-Wednesday's small fall has reversed. The wing dams and the riprap are still showing rock and the water is clear enough to fish structure rather than the slack behind it: shad are the forage, so a white or shad-pattern swimbait or a lipless crankbait worked down the face of the wing dams and along the riprap is the pattern, slowed down for water that saw another cold night, with a jig and crawfish on the slack side of the lock wall for the fish holding off the current. The R.C. Byrd tailwater itself is not gauged; this is the pool side.
waters.source: USGS 03201500 (Ohio River at Point Pleasant); config.SPORTSMAN_WATERS

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.23 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 26.02 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.2 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Normal pool and steady, 22 hundredths under the 26.45 Wednesday's paper carried and 21 hundredths over the fetcher's 24-hour comparison, so the lower gauge is moving a few inches either way around 26 feet while the upper gauge holds at 25. Below the dam the pattern is the structure the dam makes: skipjack and shad stack in the current below the gates, and a spoon or a heavy jig worked in the churn, or a live skipjack drifted along the current seams off the lock wall, is the hybrid and catfish setup; the riprap along the Huntington bank fishes a crawfish-colour jig on the slack side where the bank current breaks. Huntington is the downstream bracket, 30-odd river miles below the dam, not the tailwater reading, which the Corps publish and this pipeline cannot fetch.

waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 3:05 AM and 3:26 PM in the sound.
waters.working: All eight events land inside Thursday on both stations, the table about 50 minutes later than Wednesday's. The sound lags the surf by 41 minutes on the overnight high, 68 on the morning low, 50 on the afternoon high and 73 on the evening low, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills; the afternoon flood climbs 2.6 feet from the 9:35 low to the 3:26 high and the evening ebb drops 3.0 feet to the 10:00 low, the lowest low of the week, and at waxing gibbous, 72% and 9.5 days the moon is five days short of full, which the file's age puts on Tuesday, so the swings are building from the neap toward the spring tides. The water at Beaufort read 57.4F at 5:30 a.m., up six tenths from Wednesday's reading. The NWS active-alerts feed for North Carolina, read at 5:45 a.m., carried no product at all for the state: no frost advisory, rip current or beach hazards statement. The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report, a monthly, is dated Nov. 1 and is 18 days old, so it is the month's pattern and not this morning's conditions: East Coast Sports reports the piers taking a few big red drum of 32 inches and up on the north end, a mix of smaller red drum and the occasional speckled trout in the sound with the focus shifting to almost exclusive trout action as the weather cools; Native Son says the deeper seams of 5 to 8 feet in the main creeks are the trout target and cut bait the best bet for scattered reds; Speckled Specialist reports live shrimp under a cork in 4 to 16 feet of water, 3/16-ounce jig heads with a soft plastic for artificials and black drum to 18 inches on the same floated shrimp over structure; Carolina Flats has the reds in a last blitz on the oyster and grass banks before the bait thins; Jolly Roger Pier reports scattered speckled trout, Virginia mullet and spot at night and thick bluefish early. Tied to today's table and a sound still in the 50s, the 9:35 low falls in the cold and the window is the top of the flood and the first of the ebb, roughly 2 to 5 p.m., once the sun has been on the flats: trout in the 5-to-8-foot creek-channel seams and along the ICWW channel edge on a 3/16-ounce jig head and a small soft plastic worked slowly, or a live shrimp under a popping cork drifted over the oyster bars at the creek mouths as the water starts to leave the grass. Red drum want the last of the fall, roughly 7 to the 10:00 p.m. low, which runs well into dark, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges, or a soft plastic on the oyster and grass banks in the last of the light; the flooded-grass window for a weedless gold spoon is the hour before the 3:26 high. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel on the last of the flood; bluefish are the beach fish on a metal jig in the early morning. Flounder are release only.
